description: SpaceDragon is a solo dev project building a game-style tactical HUD for human Marswalks. Mixing real NASA planetary data with high-immersion UI design to make EVA navigation feel like a modern aerospace interface!
summary: SpaceDragon is an edge-native EVA visor HUD and autonomous rover support system engineered to revolutionize astronaut surface navigation during planetary exploration. By fusing multi-layer orbital data including HiRISE/CTX high resolution imagery, CRISM hyperspectral mineral mapping and HRSC digital elevation models, SpaceDragon projects critical terrain hazards, mineral waypoints, and safe travel paths directly into an astronaut’s field of view. Operating entirely offline on local orbital caches, the system eliminates the 4 to 24 minute Earth to Mars communication lag, empowering crewed missions to navigate treacherous terrain like Gale Crater with zero mission control dependency. SpaceDragon reduces EVA route planning delays by over 45%, providing the high efficiency situational awareness required for safe, autonomous long-duration surface operations.
details: SpaceDragon is an edge-native EVA visor HUD and autonomous rover support system built to completely transform how astronauts navigate planetary surfaces. When exploring rough terrain around locations like Gale Crater, astronauts currently rely on bulky handheld tablets and static wrist maps. More critically, the 4 to 24 minute communication delay between Earth and Mars makes real-time guidance from mission control impossible. To solve this, SpaceDragon processes multi layer orbital datasets directly on local hardware without needing an active connection. It integrates HiRISE and CTX imagery for submeter surface detail, CRISM hyperspectral data to spot high value minerals like clays and sulfates and HRSC digital elevation models to calculate safe slopes and topography. By running entirely offline on local orbital caches, the HUD projects real time hazard warnings, mineral waypoints, and safe travel paths right into the astronaut's field of view. The system cuts EVA route planning delays by over 45% and keeps astronauts' hands entirely free while automatically steering crews away from physical hazards like loose sand traps and steep channel walls. SpaceDragon is fully scalable for future lunar Artemis missions and terrestrial search and rescue operations in GPS denied zones.
